name: Tomb of Gia Long
kicker: Pine-hill tomb of the dynasty’s founder
summary: The founder’s tomb: a family of tombs spread over 42 named pine hills upstream, with no outer wall. Walk the honor court and seven terraces to Bửu Thành and the two stone tombs of the king and the empress, with Minh Thành temple beside them. Go for the dynasty’s first tomb, reached by river boat or by road and ferry.
getThere: About 18 km by boat, or about 16 km by road and the Kim Ngọc ferry, to xã Hương Thọ.
heroCaption: A yellow pavilion among the pines at Gia Long’s tomb

notice.title: Not on the four-site ticket
notice.body: The 530,000 VND four-site ticket covers the Imperial City, Minh Mang, Tu Duc, and Khai Dinh. Gia Long is a separate 150,000 VND adult ticket, and a child from 7 to 12 enters free.

body: The name covers a family of tombs, not one courtyard. Work ran from 1814 to 1820, after Empress Thừa Thiên Cao died. The centre describes more than 28 square kilometres and 42 named hills, from the Trường Sơn foothills to the Tả Trạch, in xã Hương Thọ.

Three zones make the visit. The burial of the king and the empress has an honor court, seven terraces, and Bửu Thành with two stone tombs. Minh Thành temple is on the right. A stele pavilion on the left carries Minh Mạng’s “Thánh đức thần công”. There is no outer wall. The pines are the boundary. The centre says 85 marker columns once stood, 42 remained in 1859, and two are left.

An adult ticket is 150,000 VND, and children under 13 enter free. Come by boat, about 18 km up the Perfume River to the landing, or by road, about 16 km, then the Kim Ngọc ferry and a few kilometres of forest track to the two columns.

figures.caption: Two stone tombs in the burial court
figures.alt: Two stone tombs side by side among trees at the tomb of Gia Long

gettingThere: The centre’s own route is a boat of about 18 km up the Perfume River, or a road of about 16 km and then the Kim Ngọc ferry, plus a few kilometres of forest track.

legs.heading: From the south bank
legs.body: Boat about 18 km, or road about 16 km and the Kim Ngọc ferry.

hours: 16 Mar–15 Oct: 06:30–18:00, tickets until 17:30. 16 Oct–15 Mar: 07:00–17:30, tickets until 17:00 (conservation centre notice, 12 Mar 2024). Confirm the board on arrival.
closed: No weekly closing day on the centre’s notice.
admissionNote: Adult 150,000 VND. A child from 7 to 12 is free. Under 7 is free. Hue residents and the other groups named in Resolution 55 pay half. This tomb is not on the four-site ticket.
